title: Facets measure what actually moved by diffing balances instead of trusting an integration's return values
content:
A.2.2.10.1.1.1.2.5.2.5.1.3 states that depositing into a tick range "does not necessarily use the full target amount of both tokens; the Uniswap v3 Facet measures the amounts actually deposited by comparing the ALM Proxy's token balances before and after the call, rather than relying on the target amounts or the position manager's own return values."

A.2.2.10.1.1.1.2.5.2.5.3.3 applies the same technique to swaps: the Facet "measures the amount actually sold by comparing the ALM Proxy's balance of the given token before and after the swap, and applies the Rate Limit against that measured amount rather than the specified amount."

The pattern establishes a trust boundary. Requested amounts are intentions, and a third-party contract's return values are self-reports from code outside Sky's control. Balance deltas on the ALM Proxy are the only figure the Facet can verify unilaterally, so that is the figure risk accounting is built on.

Two properties follow. Rate limits stay accurate under partial execution — an operator cannot exhaust an allowance by requesting more than the venue absorbs, nor understate consumption by requesting less. And the correctness of Sky's metering does not depend on any integration reporting honestly, which is what makes adding a new Facet a bounded review problem rather than an audit of the counterparty protocol's accounting.
description: Both the Uniswap v3 deposit and swap paths compare ALM Proxy balances before and after the call, and rate limits are charged against that measurement rather than the requested amount.
